summary: Dr. Reddy’s supplies finished medicines, ingredients for other medicine makers, research and manufacturing services, and consumer-health products.
description: The company can sell a pack of finished medicine, supply the active ingredient another manufacturer needs, or carry out agreed work for a drug developer. These are different jobs with different buyers. Its new-medicine programmes also involve research that may take time and may not reach sale.
money: Customers pay for medicines, ingredients or the services and rights in their agreements. The company pays for ingredients, people, factories, quality checks, research and getting products to buyers. Stock and unpaid customer bills can use cash before the sale is collected.
customers: Distributors, pharmacies and health systems buy finished medicines; other pharmaceutical developers and manufacturers buy ingredients or technical work. Patients use medicines, while doctors, buying organisations and the authorities that permit medicine sales influence which products can be supplied and paid for.
drivers: Actual product sales, competition and prices, permissions to sell, dependable manufacturing, delivery of contracted work, research spending and the cost of adding new businesses.

groups.title: Finished generic and biological medicines
groups.examples: Branded and unbranded generic medicines, and biosimilars in served markets.
groups.explanation: A generic is a version of an existing medicine that must meet the relevant approval standards. Biological medicines are made using living systems; a biosimilar is developed against an already approved biological medicine under a separate set of requirements. Neither is simply an ingredient sale.

groups.title: Ingredients and work for other medicine makers
groups.examples: Active ingredients and research, development and manufacturing services, including relevant Aurigene businesses.
groups.explanation: An active ingredient is the substance used for the intended effect of a medicine. A business customer may buy it or pay for a task such as developing or manufacturing a product. Payment depends on what has been supplied or completed under the contract.

groups.title: New and differentiated medicines
groups.examples: Innovative-medicine research programmes and relevant partnerships.
groups.explanation: Research is work towards a possible product. The company may still need testing, permission and a route to buyers. Announcing a programme does not mean a medicine is approved or already earning sales.

groups.title: Consumer health
groups.examples: Non-prescription and everyday health products, including acquired portfolios where rights apply.
groups.explanation: Buying a portfolio means buying a collection of products or related business rights. Dr. Reddy’s still has to arrange supply, distribution and selling in the countries covered by those rights.

basics.title: Follow what the buyer receives
basics.text: A pharmacy buying finished packs is a different customer from a manufacturer buying ingredients or a developer buying research work. Ask what is delivered, when it is accepted and when the buyer must pay before comparing these activities.

basics.title: The company must keep funding the next steps
basics.text: Research, factories and stock need money before all customer payments arrive. Selling a product at more than its manufacturing cost does not yet cover every cost of running and developing the business.

steps.title: Agree on a product or a job
steps.text: Choose a medicine or ingredient to develop, or agree the work and payment terms with a business customer.

steps.title: Develop, test and obtain permissions
steps.text: Complete the technical work, required evidence and approvals. A business customer may also need to check and accept the supplier’s process.

steps.title: Make and deliver what was promised
steps.text: Use suitable people and equipment, check quality and supply the product or completed work under the agreement.

steps.title: Collect payment and fund continuing work
steps.text: Bill and receive payment while paying suppliers, staff and other costs. Keep supporting existing products and funding further development.

specifics.title: A strong generic launch may not keep the same price
specifics.text: More competing versions or a large buyer changing suppliers can reduce earnings later. Investigate how much growth depends on particular products and whether alternatives are entering.

specifics.title: Buying a business adds more than sales
specifics.text: An acquired portfolio can bring new customers, but also purchase payments, integration work and borrowing costs. Amortisation means spreading the accounting cost of certain purchased rights over their useful life; it can reduce later profit without being a fresh purchase payment each time.

specifics.title: An announced service contract still needs delivery
specifics.text: Research or manufacturing work may be paid in stages. A milestone is an agreed condition, such as completing a task, that can trigger payment. Check what work is done rather than treating the whole announced contract value as sales already earned.

watch: What is driving growth in products and markets?
New launches and purchased businesses can change the total differently.
Read the business reviews for the same period and currency. Separate products already sold before an acquisition from sales added by the acquired business, where the company explains them.
Can important generic products keep earning?
Competition can change prices after launch.
Check which products matter most, whether new alternatives are entering and what the company says about prices and supply. Permission to sell is different from actual customer purchases.
Are factories able to deliver reliably?
Quality restrictions can affect particular products or countries.
Read official findings and company responses by site and date. Check what changes are required and whether the regulator has confirmed that restrictions were resolved.
What has expansion and research cost so far?
A larger product list does not prove the spending is worthwhile.

Read purchase payments, integration work, research spending and later charges for purchased rights. Goodwill is the purchase price left after identifying the acquired net assets; a later write-down can signal that expectations were too high.
Are completed sales and services being paid for?
Stock and unpaid bills can absorb cash despite profit.
Compare cash from daily operations with customer amounts due, stock and contract payments. Keep profit after all group costs separate from earlier measures such as gross profit.
risks: More competitors or different purchasing decisions can weaken sales from important products.
Factory findings, restrictions or input shortages can interrupt sales and launches.
Development work does not reach a successful sale
Testing, permissions or demand may fail to support the spending.
Expansion and overseas operations bring other costs
Integrating acquired products, disputes over intellectual property and changes in exchange rates can affect earnings and cash.
context: When one large product fades, look at the rest

Lenalidomide is Dr. Reddy’s generic version of the brand-name medicine Revlimid. The company launched it in the US in 2022 with limits on the quantity it could sell. In its 23 October 2026 results presentation, Dr. Reddy’s said total sales for July–September 2026 were slightly lower than a year earlier because lenalidomide sales fell. Sales excluding lenalidomide in North America, which the company calls its base business, grew by a double-digit percentage, meaning 10 percent or more. The same update says some batches of an ingredient called semaglutide did not meet their required quality standard and that the company is working to resolve this. Ask whether the remaining products can replace a fading product’s sales and profit, and whether quality problems delay new ones.
quiz: Is supplying an ingredient the same transaction as selling a finished medicine?
No. An ingredient is an input another manufacturer uses. A finished medicine is supplied in its approved form for use. The buyer, required work and cost of reaching that buyer can differ.
sources: Lenalidomide decline, base business and semaglutide quality issue · results presentation 23 October 2026

financialNotes.title: Keep the source segment definitions
financialNotes.text: The table follows the audited IFRS segment note and shows external revenue with segment gross profit. Gross profit still has to cover research, selling and other later costs; it is not segment net profit. Internal PSAI sales are excluded from the displayed revenue, and geographical or therapeutic sales must not be added to it as separate businesses.
